sections.html: South America: Colombia, Rio Magdalena and Rio Cauca. Type locality: Aus dem Cauca, dem grössten Nebenflusse des Magdalenen-Stromes, Colombia.
Wood eaters of this size (more than 40 cm) need large aquariums with very high-performance filtration units, since substantial quantities of excrement are produced.
This species is a bit robust in an aquarium set-up so would need plenty of hiding places, plenty of water changes, due to their wood eating habits, and powerful filtration. Needs a spacious aquarium.
The vegetable part of the food should be high; cucumbers, potatoes, carrots and other vegetables are gladly eaten.
All Panaque (Panaqolus) are wood eaters so would need this in an aquarium set-up. Feed also vegetable foods such as cucumber, courgette (zucchini) and sinking tablets.
Breeding attempts would be interesting to secure the species' existence in aquariums. However, even in former years, when they were not so rare, no confirmed breeding reports are known.

This catfish was for many years thought to be Panaque suttonorum (suttoni?) but it is now finally recognised to be Panaque cochliodon. This mistake was rectified when again looking at Schultz's original description of P. suttonorum, which was totally different, and was also from a different location. The smaller Panaques are actually Panaqolus and the larger species are Panaque.

Description: Panaque have an oval shaped mouth and the jaws have very large spatulate teeth with a single cusp, arranged in a V form, while Panaqolus have a small number of spatulate teeth and Panaque grow quite a bit larger.

Etymology: The specific name cochliodon: cochli, from cochlearium (L.), a small Roman spoon with a long tapering handle; odon, from odoús, tooth, referring to spoon-shaped dentary and premaxillary tooth cusps.

Known for its blue eyes.

IUCN Red List: Near Threatened because of a suspected population reduction of approximately 25% due to fishing pressure for ornamental purposes and habitat degradation in parts of its range. It may qualify for Vulnerable, but there are currently not sufficient data to support such an assessment. Surveys to estimate population size and monitor trends are recommended (IUCN 2016).

photos.author: Sini Merikallio from Helsinki, Finland
photos.caption: I named him Rambo. He came with the aquarium I bought when 10 years old or so, he was already big. When I was about 17 he died, shortly after which I sold my aquarium as he was 'the fish of my life'.
